Test beta diversity for associations with metadata.

Source: R/stats_table.r
bdiv_stats.Rd

Pairwise distances are not independent observations, so beta diversity is tested with permutation tests in which samples, not distances, are permuted: PERMANOVA and friends for a categorical stat.by, or a Mantel test for a numeric regr. See distmat_stats() for the tests.

Usage

bdiv_stats(
  biom,
  regr = NULL,
  stat.by = NULL,
  bdiv = "bray",
  weighted = NULL,
  tree = NULL,
  within = NULL,
  between = NULL,
  split.by = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  test = if (is.null(regr)) "adonis2" else "mantel",
  seed = 0,
  permutations = 999,
  p.adj = "fdr",
  alpha = 0.5,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

biom

An rbiom object, or any value accepted by as_rbiom().

regr

Dataset field with a numeric variable to correlate the distances with (Mantel test). When both regr and stat.by are given, the Mantel test is run within each stat.by group. Default: NULL

stat.by

Dataset field with the groups to compare. Must be categorical. Any ==/!= prefix is ignored. Default: NULL

bdiv

Beta diversity distance algorithm(s) to use. Options are: c("aitchison", "bhattacharyya", "bray", "canberra", "chebyshev", "chord", "clark", "sorensen", "divergence", "euclidean", "generalized_unifrac", "gower", "hamming", "hellinger", "horn", "jaccard", "jensen", "jsd", "lorentzian", "manhattan", "matusita", "minkowski", "morisita", "motyka", "normalized_unifrac", "ochiai", "psym_chisq", "soergel", "squared_chisq", "squared_chord", "squared_euclidean", "topsoe", "unweighted_unifrac", "variance_adjusted_unifrac", "wave_hedges", "weighted_unifrac"). For the UniFrac family, a phylogenetic tree must be present in biom or explicitly provided via tree=. Supports partial matching. Multiple values are allowed for functions which return a table or plot. Default: "bray"

weighted

(Deprecated - weighting is now inherent in bdiv metric name.) Take relative abundances into account. When weighted=FALSE, only presence/absence is considered. Multiple values allowed. Default: NULL

tree

A phylo object representing the phylogenetic relationships of the taxa in biom. Only required when computing UniFrac distances. Default: biom$tree

within, between

Accepted for compatibility with bdiv_table() and bdiv_boxplot(), where they select which sample pairs are displayed. The tests here are computed on samples, so these arguments have no effect.

split.by

Dataset field(s) that the data should be split by prior to any calculations. Must be categorical. Default: NULL

strata

Dataset field with a blocking variable, such as a subject identifier for repeated measures. Must be categorical. When stat.by (or regr) varies within strata, permutations are restricted to within each stratum; when it is constant within every stratum (a between-subject variable), whole strata are permuted instead. See the Details of distmat_stats(). test = "mrpp" and "betadisper" are not available for a between-strata variable. Default: NULL

test

The permutation test. With stat.by: "adonis2" (PERMANOVA; the default), "mrpp", or "betadisper" (homogeneity of dispersion). With regr: "mantel" (the default) or "adonis2" (PERMANOVA with a numeric covariate). See distmat_stats().

seed

Random seed for permutations, rarefaction, random tie-breaking, and stochastic ordinations. Results are reproducible for a given seed, and the caller's random number generator state is left unchanged. Must be a non-negative integer. Default: 0

permutations

Number of random permutations to use. Default: 999

p.adj

Method to use for multiple comparisons adjustment of p-values. Run p.adjust.methods for a list of available options. The adjustment spans the entire returned table. Default: "fdr"

alpha

The alpha term to use in Generalized UniFrac. How much weight to give to relative abundances; a value between 0 and 1, inclusive. Setting alpha=1 is equivalent to Normalized UniFrac. Default: 0.5

cpus

The number of CPUs to use. Set to NULL to use all available, or to 1 to disable parallel processing. Does not affect results. Default: ecodive::n_cpus() (all available cores)

Value

A tibble data.frame with one row per test. With a categorical stat.by and more than two groups, each split.by stratum (and bdiv metric) gets an omnibus test across all groups plus one pairwise test per pair of groups, computed on that pair's samples. The columns are:

split.by fields, .bdiv -

The stratum. .bdiv is only present when several bdiv metrics were requested.

stat.by field -

The groups compared, joined by " vs ". The omnibus row lists all groups.

.groups -

The number of groups in the comparison: 2 for pairwise rows, more for the omnibus row.

.n, .stat, .r.sqr, .z, .p.val -

See distmat_stats().

.adj.p -

.p.val adjusted for multiple comparisons across the whole table.

With a numeric regr, one Mantel test per stratum, with .n, .stat (Spearman's r), .p.val, and .adj.p. The R code used to compute the table is in $code.

Details

With strata (e.g. repeated samples per subject), the permutation scheme depends on the variable being tested. A variable that varies within strata (e.g. time point) is permuted within each stratum. A variable that is constant within every stratum (e.g. delivery mode, with subject as the stratum) is permuted at the stratum level: whole strata exchange their values, so the effective sample size is the number of strata. When the number of distinct arrangements is no larger than permutations, all of them are enumerated and the p-value is exact. The scheme is chosen separately for each row of the table (a pair of groups can be a between-strata comparison even when the omnibus test is not) and is reported in the table header. See distmat_stats() for details.

See also

Other beta_diversity: bdiv_boxplot(), bdiv_clusters(), bdiv_corrplot(), bdiv_heatmap(), bdiv_ord_plot(), bdiv_ord_table(), bdiv_table(), distmat_stats()

Other stats_tables: adiv_stats(), distmat_stats(), stats_table(), taxa_stats()

Examples

    library(rbiom)

    biom <- rarefy(hmp50)

    bdiv_stats(biom, stat.by = "Sex", bdiv = c("bray", "w_unifrac"))
#> # Test:     PERMANOVA ~ Sex; 999 permutations.
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   .bdiv            Sex            .groups    .n .stat .r.sqr .p.val .adj.p
#>   <chr>            <chr>            <int> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 weighted_unifrac Female vs Male       2    49  2.19 0.0444  0.075  0.088
#> 2 bray             Female vs Male       2    49  1.62 0.0332  0.088  0.088

    biom <- subset(biom, `Body Site` %in% c('Saliva', 'Stool', 'Buccal mucosa'))
    bdiv_stats(biom, stat.by = "Body Site", split.by = "Sex")
#> # Test:     PERMANOVA ~ `Body Site`; 999 permutations.
#> # A tibble: 8 × 8
#>   Sex    `Body Site`                    .groups    .n .stat .r.sqr .p.val .adj.p
#>   <fct>  <chr>                            <int> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 Female Buccal mucosa vs Saliva vs St…       3    15 14.0   0.701  0.001  0.004
#> 2 Male   Buccal mucosa vs Saliva vs St…       3    14 10.1   0.647  0.001  0.004
#> 3 Female Saliva vs Stool                      2    10 10.6   0.569  0.007  0.016
#> 4 Male   Buccal mucosa vs Stool               2     9 11.8   0.627  0.011  0.016
#> 5 Female Buccal mucosa vs Stool               2    10 16.7   0.675  0.012  0.016
#> 6 Male   Saliva vs Stool                      2     9 11.7   0.625  0.013  0.016
#> 7 Female Buccal mucosa vs Saliva              2    10 17.9   0.691  0.016  0.016
#> 8 Male   Buccal mucosa vs Saliva              2    10  6.37  0.443  0.016  0.016

    bdiv_stats(biom, regr = "Age")
#> # Test:     Mantel (Spearman) ~ Age; 999 permutations.
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>      .n   .stat .p.val .adj.p
#>   <int>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1    29 0.00817  0.399  0.399

    # Repeated measures: delivery mode is constant within each subject,
    # so whole subjects are permuted.
    b <- rarefy(subset(babies, `Age (days)` <= 30))
    bdiv_stats(b, stat.by = "Delivery mode", strata = "Subject ID")
#> # Test:     PERMANOVA ~ `Delivery mode`; whole `Subject ID` strata permuted
#> #   (between-strata variable; all 220 arrangements, exact).
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   `Delivery mode`     .groups    .n .stat .r.sqr .p.val .adj.p
#>   <chr>                 <int> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 Cesarean vs Vaginal       2   360  9.17 0.0250    0.5    0.5
